meta.about: Incorporated in 1981, Paradeep Phosphates Limited is a manufacturer of non-urea fertilizers and India’s second largest private sector phosphatic company. The company is engaged in manufacturing, trading, distribution, and sales of a variety of complex fertilizers such as DAP, three grades of Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium (namely NPK-10, NPK-12, and NP-20), Zypmite, Phospho-gypsum, and Hydroflorosilicic Acid.[1]
meta.keyPoints: Promoter[1] [2] The company is promoted by Zuari Agro Chemicals and OCP Group of Morocco, jointly holding 56% through Zuari Maroc Phosphates Pvt Ltd. The OCP Group is one of the world's largest phosphatic players, with a sizeable control over the world’s known phosphate reserves.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Paradeep Phosphates (consolidated incl. MCFL, ₹ crore). One reported segment, so the engine runs on revenue growth and EBITDA margin; both come from the business build below (tonnes sold × revenue per tonne; EBITDA per tonne), which the authoring script checks against the model. EBITDA is Screener's basis (excludes other income), ~₹50-100/t below the company's 'EBITDA per tonne', which includes other income. Net-debt company: no treasury yield, explicit finance cost. Valued on Sep-28E P/E (the street's latest method), with EV/EBITDA and DCF (at a WACC) as cross-checks.

build._why: Volumes: FY26 4.21 mt (manufactured 3.57, traded 0.64); Q1FY27 0.985 mt (+4.7%; manufactured 0.86, traded 0.13). FY27: plants run near 70% of phosphoric-acid capacity while sulphur and ammonia are scarce, so manufactured volume slips to ~3.40 mt despite the 0.3 mt granulation debottleneck from Dec-2026; ~0.5 mt of imports secured for rabi lift traded volume to ~0.95 mt. FY28: capacity 4.0 mt and phosphoric acid 0.7 mt from Aug-Sep 2027, manufactured 3.85 mt, trading back to ~0.70 mt. FY29: manufactured 4.05 mt (the debottlenecked 4.0 mt run fully plus a little from the 1.0 mt granulation train, guided for around Q2FY29-FY30), traded 0.75 mt. Revenue per tonne: FY26 ₹51,845, Q1FY27 ₹62,165 (NPK prices +₹400-500 a bag, Kharif NBS +10%, more DAP and imports); FY27 ₹61,000; FY28-29 ₹58,000 as input prices ease partly. EBITDA per tonne (Screener basis): FY25 ₹4,120, FY26 ₹5,245, Q1FY27 ₹7,309 on low-cost stock. FY27 ₹4,900, a touch under management's 'realistic ~₹5,000', because Q2 buys sulphur at $1,000+ and acid at $1,700 against an unchanged Kharif subsidy, rabi rates were unknown and trading (~₹2,000/t) is a bigger share. FY28 ₹5,400 (phase-1 acid, Goa energy savings, debottlenecked volumes) and FY29 ₹5,800: well short of management's ₹6,500-7,000+ after full integration, which needs the big project and normal raw-material prices.

assumptions._revenueWhy: From the build: 4.35 mt × ₹61,000 = ₹26,535 cr (FY27E, +21.6%); 4.55 mt × ₹58,000 = ₹26,390 cr (FY28E, −0.5%); 4.80 mt × ₹58,000 = ₹27,840 cr (FY29E, +5.5%). Price, not volume, drives FY27; volume drives FY29.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 cash capex ₹868 cr (sulphuric acid plants, Goa energy project). FY27 ₹800 cr: '~₹600 cr' normal capex incl. some major-project outflow (CFO, May-2026), ₹600-700 cr per the Jun-2026 plant visit, plus the first ~₹100 cr of the ₹250 cr aluminium fluoride plant. FY28-29 ₹1,600 cr and ₹1,500 cr: most of the ₹3,600 cr programme (1.0 mt granulation, 0.3 mt phosphoric acid with matching sulphuric acid) plus the rest of aluminium fluoride and ~₹200 cr a year of maintenance. Management funds new projects ~70% with debt.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹403 cr = 5.8% of average gross block (₹6,944 cr); Q4FY26 ₹126 cr and Q1FY27 ₹106 cr (~₹424 cr a year) after the new sulphuric acid plants. The engine holds CWIP flat and depreciates capex at once, but most FY28-29 capex is construction work in progress that earns no depreciation until the big project is commissioned (Q2FY29-FY30), so we use 5.3%: ~₹421 / ₹485 / ₹567 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net-debt company: borrowings ₹6,872 cr plus ₹34 cr of leases at Mar-2026 against cash, bank balances and liquid funds of ₹409 cr (net debt ~₹6,500 cr). Interest income is built into other income below, not earned on a treasury book.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, Screener basis (which nets the loss on discarded plant). FY26 company other income ₹147 cr = interest ₹29 cr (bank ₹12 cr, tax refund ₹3 cr, other ₹14 cr) + mutual-fund gains ₹59 cr (parking subsidy receipts) + rent ₹5 cr + miscellaneous ₹50 cr + write-backs ₹4 cr; Screener shows ₹88 cr 'normal' after netting ₹56 cr of plant-discard loss. FY27E ₹85 cr = interest ₹20 cr (cash fell from ₹1,036 cr to ₹392 cr) + fund gains ₹30 cr (smaller surpluses with debt up) + rent and miscellaneous ₹55 cr − discard losses ₹20 cr; write-backs excluded. Check: Q1FY27 normal other income ₹21.6 cr (×4 = ₹86 cr); TTM normal ₹134 cr before Screener's annual netting of discard losses. FY29E ₹90 cr. The +₹21.8 cr Q1FY27 exceptional (Labour Code reversal) is excluded.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (interest, bank charges, exchange loss on foreign-currency borrowings)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹528 cr = interest ₹333 cr + exchange loss on buyer's credit ₹145 cr + bank charges ₹45 cr + tax interest ₹4 cr; Q1FY27 ₹132 cr (~₹527 cr a year) on gross debt of ₹6,500 cr. FY27E ₹540 cr: debt stays high with subsidy receivables at ₹4,600 cr and costlier imports; we assume a smaller exchange loss than FY26. FY28E ₹520 cr: working capital eases but project debt builds, with interest during construction capitalised. FY29E ₹545 cr as project debt peaks (~5.8% on ~₹8,500 cr plus ~₹50 cr of bank charges and ~₹30 cr of exchange cost, less capitalised interest).
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 25.0% (FY26), 25.4% (Q1FY27); new-regime statutory rate 25.17%. Paradeep's merged entity has no minorities (MCFL merged, not a subsidiary), so model EPS = profit ÷ 103.75 cr shares (actual 103.82 cr).
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹1.50 a share (15.6% of EPS); FY25 ₹1.00. Capex years: we assume 15%.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts free cash flow at one rate and labels it the cost of equity. Paradeep carries ~₹6,500-7,500 cr of net debt against a market value of ~₹16,000 cr, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1: subsidy-policy and raw-material risk plus leverage) weighted ~70%, post-tax cost of debt ~6.0% (8% pre-tax at the margin) weighted ~30% = ~11.0%, which is what beta 0.75 produces. The same rate rolls the value forward six months.
dcf._tgWhy: Phosphatic fertiliser demand grows ~2-3% a year in volume plus price; 5.5% nominal in rupees.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~5.5% (FY29E) to 6% by year 12: ~2-3% volume (the 1.0 mt granulation train and acid expansion fill, then market growth) plus ~3% price.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin drifts from 10.0% (FY29E) to 10.5% (~₹6,100/t on ₹58,000/t) as integration completes; policy (NBS, reasonable-margin rules) keeps it below management's ₹7,000/t aspiration.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~5.4% of revenue (FY29E, big project) to 3%, above depreciation at 2.2% to fund volume growth.
dcf._yearsWhy: 12-year explicit/fade period so the FY28-29 project spend is followed by the years in which it earns.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Rabi and FY28 subsidy rates cover the Middle East cost spike, sulphur and ammonia normalise, the big project lands on time and integration lifts EBITDA towards ₹6,500/t by FY29 (management's path); volumes grow faster with the new granulation train.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Subsidy rates lag input costs for another year, sulphur stays above $1,000/t, trading is a larger share, the big project slips and the government tightens reasonable-margin rules: EBITDA stays near ~₹4,500-5,000/t while debt keeps rising.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Paradeep now: Prabhudas Lilladher 13x FY28E EPS (Accumulate, ₹158, 31-Jul-2026; 10-11x in Mar-Jun 2026). 9.5x is derived: the stock's one-year-forward P/E median since listing (May-2022) is 11.6x after putting FY25 EPS on the merger-consistent basis and leaving out the FY24 trough year (10.9x on Screener's unadjusted EPS); seven listed fertiliser peers traded a median 17% below their five-year median P/E on 30-Sep-2026, so 11.6x × 0.83 ≈ 9.6x, rounded to 9.5x. No premium for growth: EPS compounds ~10% a year FY26-29E, ROE (~14%) only matches the ~13% cost of equity and net debt stays near 3x EBITDA. Bull 13x (the street's multiple: the market keeps paying for the integration story); bear 8x (where Chambal, GNFC and GSFC trade: a plain, indebted fertiliser maker under subsidy stress).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Elara Capital's method (8.0x FY28E, May-2026). Paradeep's trailing EV/EBITDA median since listing is 10.0x outside the FY24 trough window; peers traded a median 5% below their five-year EV/EBITDA, i.e. ~9.5x trailing, which on Sep-28E EBITDA (~14% above the trailing twelve months) is ~8.3x: we use 8x and deduct Sep-28E net debt (~₹7,800 cr).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: FCFF FY28-FY39E with revenue growth fading to 6%, EBITDA margin to 10.5%, capex to 3% of revenue and working capital at the FY26 ratio (31% of revenue), discounted at an 11% WACC (entered as beta 0.75), terminal growth 5.5%, less Mar-27E net debt.

cover.headline: A good phosphate franchise with OCP behind it, a squeezed FY27 and a stretched balance sheet, priced for the integration payoff before it arrives
cover.lead: Paradeep is India's second-largest private phosphatic fertiliser maker: 3.7 mt of DAP, NPK and urea capacity at Paradeep (Odisha), Goa and Mangalore, with Morocco's OCP as co-promoter and main supplier. The MCFL merger (effective Oct-2025, 22.2 cr new shares) added the Mangalore plant and the south. Q1FY27 was a record (PAT ₹393 cr, EBITDA ~₹7,300/t) because the company had bought raw materials before the Middle East crisis; management itself calls ~₹5,000/t realistic for FY27, and rabi subsidy rates were unknown on 30-Sep. Net debt was ~₹6,500 cr at Mar-2026 with ₹3,600 cr of projects ahead. We value Paradeep the way the street now does, on **P/E: 9.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹11.9**, which gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** EV/EBITDA (₹127) and DCF (₹73) also sit below the ₹154 share price. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Policy sets the margin, and FY27 is a squeeze year
arguments.p: About 53% of FY26 revenue was government subsidy. Kharif 2026 NBS rates rose ~10% while sulphur went from ~$850/t (Q1 average) to $1,000+ and the phosphoric acid contract from ~$1,360 to $1,700/t. Q1's ₹7,309/t EBITDA came from cheap opening stock. We model ₹4,900/t for FY27 (management: ~₹5,000), so EPS falls 6% to ₹9.1 even with Q1 banked.

arguments.h: Integration is the right plan, but it is debt-funded and keeps slipping
arguments.p: The ₹3,600 cr programme (phosphoric acid 0.5 → 1.0 mt, more sulphuric acid, 1.0 mt granulation) should lift EBITDA per tonne by 30-35%. Timing moved from 'end-FY28' to 'around Q2FY29-FY30'. We model ~₹3,900 cr of capex in FY27-29E on top of working capital at 31% of revenue: net debt ~₹7,500 cr at Mar-27E (3.5x EBITDA). arguments.p: OCP companies supplied ~₹8,200 cr of rock, acid, TSP and DAP in FY26 (about half of purchases): when sulphur and ammonia ran short in 2026, Paradeep still had rock and acid. arguments.p: Prabhudas Lilladher values the stock at 13x FY28E EPS of ₹12.6; our FY28E EPS is ₹11.1 (-12%). Paradeep's one-year-forward P/E median since listing is 11.6x (on merger-consistent EPS, trough year excluded); fertiliser peers trade 17% below their own medians, giving ~9.5x. sections.title: Three port-based plants that turn imported rock, acid, sulphur and ammonia into DAP, NPK and urea

blocks.p: Paradeep makes and sells phosphatic fertilisers (DAP and NPK "complex" grades, led by NPK 20:20:0:13) and urea from three coastal plants, and imports DAP, TSP, MOP and ammonium sulphate to sell alongside. It reports a single segment. FY26: 3.67 mt produced (~100% of capacity), 4.21 mt sold (3.57 mt manufactured, 0.64 mt traded), of which NPK incl. TSP 2.46 mt, DAP 0.76 mt and urea 0.84 mt. It sells through ~7,000 dealers and ~1,00,000 retailers in 18 states under the Jai Kisaan Navratna and Mangala brands. Small industrial lines (phospho-gypsum, Zypmite soil conditioner, fluorosilicic acid, ammonium bicarbonate) round it out.

blocks.p: **DAP and NPKs are a regulated conversion business.** Paradeep buys rock phosphate and phosphoric acid (mostly from OCP), sulphur and ammonia (imported), converts them and sells at a maximum retail price that is capped in practice: DAP at ₹1,350 a 50 kg bag, NPKs at ₹2,100-2,500 in mid-2026. The government pays a subsidy per kg of nitrogen, phosphorus, potash and sulphur (the Nutrient Based Subsidy, NBS), reset every kharif (Apr-Sep) and rabi (Oct-Mar) season, plus a special top-up on DAP. Profit per tonne = farm price + subsidy − raw-material and conversion cost. When raw materials jump faster than the subsidy, margins shrink; when policy catches up, they recover. **Urea** is fully controlled: the government pays cost plus a return under energy norms, so profit depends on plant efficiency, not prices (Goa improved from 6.4 to 6.1 Gcal/t). **Trading** imported DAP/TSP earns ~₹2,000/t against ₹6,000-7,000/t for integrated manufacturing (management).

sections.title: Indian phosphatics: steady demand, imported inputs, and a subsidy that sets the margin

blocks.p: India uses ~24 mt of phosphatic fertilisers a year: ~10 mt of DAP and ~14 mt of NPK complexes, of which the 20:20:0:13 grade, Paradeep's lead product, is 6-7 mt. Demand grows slowly (farmer-level sales +~1% in Q1FY27) and depends on the monsoon and on farm prices. Two features set the economics. **Inputs are imported:** India buys most of its rock phosphate, much of its phosphoric acid and most of its sulphur and ammonia abroad, and 70-75% of world sulphur and ammonia trade passes the Strait of Hormuz, which the 2026 Middle East crisis disrupted. **The margin is a policy outcome:** the government fixes the NBS subsidy per kg of nutrient each season and holds the DAP price at ₹1,350 a bag, so in a cost spike it decides how much the industry absorbs. In Q1FY27 industry DAP+NPK production fell 21% and imports 38% because Kharif rates (+~10%) did not cover the cost jump (Coromandel's Q1 call).

bullets: **Volume and share.** Manufactured phosphatic sales (DAP + NPK + SSP) were 2.72 mt in FY26 (Q2FY26 alone 0.78 mt); with traded DAP and TSP, DAP was 0.76 mt and NPK incl. TSP 2.46 mt. It runs its plants at ~100% of capacity in normal years (3.67 mt produced in FY26).

**Mix moves with policy.** In Q1FY27 DAP sales rose 55% and NPKs fell 9%: with DAP held at ₹1,350 a bag and topped up by the government, DAP was more profitable than NPKs, whose prices had to rise ₹400-500 a bag. Management calls this a "small-term tactical shift"; farmers return to NPKs when the bag-price gap narrows to ~₹200 (from ~₹1,000).

**Margins.** Company-stated EBITDA per tonne was ₹5,300 in FY26 (₹4,700 in Q3, ₹5,700 in Q4) and ~₹7,000 in Q1FY27 on cheap stock. Management's FY27 guide is ~₹5,000; we use ₹4,900 on the Screener basis.

**Inputs.** Paradeep is "almost fully" integrated in phosphoric and sulphuric acid at its own site; Goa and Mangalore buy phosphoric acid (both make their own ammonia from gas). Sulphur is bought spot ($1,000+ at end-July); 20-30% of Paradeep's sulphur and all of Mangalore's come from Indian refineries (IOC, MRPL). Rock and acid come mostly from OCP.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** a well-run, share-gaining phosphate maker with no pricing power. Our build takes total volume from 4.21 mt to 4.35 / 4.55 / 4.8 mt (FY27-29E) and EBITDA per tonne to ₹4,900 / ₹5,400 / ₹5,800: FY27 absorbs the cost spike and a heavier trading mix; FY28-29 gain from phase-1 acid and debottlenecking, but stay below management's ₹7,000+ until the big project runs. Every ₹500/t of EBITDA moves FY28E EPS by ~₹1.6 (~15%).

sections.title: Urea and trading: a steady cost-plus line and a low-margin buffer

blocks.p: **Urea (~0.8 mt a year at Goa and Mangalore).** Urea prices and costs are controlled: gas is a pass-through (~$14/MMBtu in Q4FY26, $18-19 in May-2026) and the government pays a return under plant energy norms. Profit therefore comes from efficiency. Goa's energy-saving project (6.4 → 6.1 Gcal/t, phase 1 done, phase 2 commissioning, phase 3 in H1FY29) is worth ₹1,000-1,200/t; under the norms announced on 30-Jul-2026 Goa gains ~₹1,500/t and Mangalore loses ₹700-800/t (management). Mangalore earns ~₹6,000-6,500/t after a naphtha-to-gas incentive (worth ~₹3,000/t) expired. Urea sales were 0.84 mt in FY26 and 0.20 mt in Q1FY27 (−16%; the Goa energy-project shutdown ran from February to late April 2026); with supportive policy each plant can make 0.44-0.45 mt.

**Trading (0.64 mt in FY26, 0.13 mt in Q1FY27).** Paradeep imports DAP, TSP, MOP and ammonium sulphate (largely from OCP companies and Kofert) to fill its portfolio and, in 2026, to cover lost production. Management secured ~0.5 mt of imports for rabi and says trading will be "significantly higher" than last rabi's ~0.27 mt. Trading earns ~₹2,000/t, a third of manufacturing, so a bigger trading share dilutes EBITDA per tonne even if total volume rises; we model 0.95 mt of trading in FY27.

sections.title: Backward integration: the right strategy, funded with debt and running late

blocks.p: The plan is to make all three sites self-sufficient in phosphoric and sulphuric acid and to add granulation. Done: 0.6 mt of sulphuric acid (Paradeep Sep-2025, Mangalore Mar-2026), a 350 TPD evaporator (Dec-2025) and Goa energy phase 1. Next: phosphoric acid phase 1 (0.5 → 0.6 mt by Dec-2026, 0.7 mt by Aug-Sep 2027) and granulation debottlenecking (3.7 → 4.0 mt, Dec-2026). Then the ₹3,600 cr programme announced in Nov-2025: a 1.0 mt granulation train at Paradeep, 0.3 mt more phosphoric acid with matching sulphuric acid, and more sulphuric acid at Mangalore. In Nov-2025 management said this would be complete by end-FY28; in Jul-2026 it said "one shot", around Q2FY29-FY30, with "final commercial discussions" still going on. Separately, a ₹250 cr aluminium fluoride plant was approved in Q1FY27.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Paradeep has a **narrow but real advantage in supply**: OCP, the world's largest phosphate producer, is a co-promoter and its biggest supplier, and its main plant sits on a port with its own berth and pipelines. In 2026 that kept rock and acid flowing when peers cut output, and it has let Paradeep gain share in NPKs. It does **not** give pricing power (the government sets the subsidy and, in effect, the price), its acid integration is still partial, and it carries ~₹6,500 cr of net debt where Coromandel and Chambal hold net cash. Expect mid-teens ROE through the cycle at best, with big swings, not a compounding franchise.

sections.title: Revenue up five times since FY19, mostly bought and priced in; profit per tonne is the number to watch

blocks.p: Paradeep's revenue rose from ₹4,358 cr in FY19 to ₹21,826 cr in FY26. Three things did it, and only one is organic: (1) the Goa plant bought from Zuari Agro Chemicals in June 2022 (FY23 revenue +70%); (2) the merger of Mangalore Chemicals & Fertilizers, which added ~₹3,100 cr of revenue in FY25 (the restated FY25 is ₹16,959 cr against ₹13,820 cr for Paradeep alone); and (3) fertiliser prices and subsidies, which follow world raw materials (FY23 up, FY24 down 13%, FY26 up 29%). EBITDA went from ₹452 cr to ₹2,208 cr and net profit from ₹159 cr to ₹996 cr. Per share the record is bumpier: EPS ₹6.92 (FY22, before the IPO), ₹3.73, ₹1.23 (FY24, the trough), ₹6.39 (FY25 restated) and ₹9.60 (FY26). Q1FY27 profit rose 24% to ₹393 cr on cheap opening stock.

sections.title: Earnings quality: a clean audit, but subsidy-heavy, restated, and with big related-party flows

bullets: **Subsidy is 53% of revenue.** ₹11,625 cr of FY26 revenue (incl. ₹2,088 cr on traded goods) is government subsidy, booked at notified rates on sale; the auditor (B S R & Co., KPMG network) makes it a key audit matter. Cash lags: ₹3,847 cr owed at Mar-2026 and ₹4,600 cr at Jun-2026, funded with short-term debt.

**FY25 is restated, and the merger was not accounted the usual way.** The NCLT scheme set the appointed date at 1-Apr-2024, so FY25 includes MCFL; the auditor's emphasis of matter notes that Ind AS 103 alone would have consolidated MCFL only from 16-Oct-2025. The purchase-price allocation is still provisional (goodwill ₹139 cr). Comparisons with FY24 and earlier are not like-for-like.

**Exchange losses sit in finance cost.** ₹145 cr of FY26 finance cost (₹46 cr in FY25) is exchange loss on dollar buyer's credit for imports, plus ₹50 cr of other exchange loss in other expenses. A weaker rupee hits profit below EBITDA, where EBITDA-per-tonne comparisons miss it.

**One-offs both ways.** FY26: −₹39 cr Labour Code charge (exceptional) and a ₹56 cr loss on discarded plant (Screener nets it in other income); Q1FY27: +₹21.8 cr reversal of part of the Labour Code charge. FY26 other income included ₹59 cr of mutual-fund gains on parked subsidy cash.
**Inventory gains flatter good quarters.** Q1FY27 EBITDA of ~₹7,300/t was "mainly on account of the stock" bought before prices rose (management). These gains reverse when prices fall.

**Related-party purchases.** OCP group companies supplied ~₹8,200 cr in FY26 (~half of purchases) and Zuari FarmHub (Adventz) bought ₹309 cr of fertilisers; the Goa plant (2022), MCFL (2025) and the Mahad SSP plant (2025) were all bought from group companies. Pricing is at contract terms, but minority holders depend on these being arm's length.
**Cash conversion is weak.** Operating cash over FY19-26 totalled ~₹1,500 cr against ~₹3,000 cr of cumulative net profit (plus ~₹1,450 cr of depreciation); FY26 was −₹1,012 cr.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit is clean (Big-4-network auditor, contingent liabilities ~₹160 cr, no qualification), and the restatement is disclosed in detail. But half of revenue is a policy payment, FY25 is restated under an NCLT override, exchange losses and inventory gains move profit, cash conversion is poor, and the biggest supplier is a shareholder.

sections.title: Net debt ~₹6,500 cr, and the government is the biggest debtor

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Paradeep owed ₹6,872 cr of borrowings (₹6,057 cr short-term, mostly working-capital lines and buyer's credit for imports) plus ₹34 cr of leases, against cash, bank balances and liquid funds of ₹409 cr: net debt ~₹6,500 cr, up from ~₹3,800 cr a year earlier. Two things it does not control drive this. The government owed it ₹3,847 cr of subsidy at Mar-2026 (₹2,357 cr a year earlier) and ₹4,600 cr at Jun-2026. And management deliberately bought ~30 extra days of raw materials before the Middle East crisis (inventory ₹4,627 cr vs ₹2,556 cr), which it says unwound in Q1FY27, cutting gross debt to ~₹6,500 cr by June. ICRA rates the company AA- (Stable), upgraded during FY26.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Paradeep Phosphates (consolidated incl. MCFL, ₹ crore). One reported segment, so the engine runs on revenue growth and EBITDA margin; both come from the business build below (tonnes sold × revenue per tonne; EBITDA per tonne), which the authoring script checks against the model. EBITDA is Screener's basis (excludes other income), ~₹50-100/t below the company's 'EBITDA per tonne', which includes other income. Net-debt company: no treasury yield, explicit finance cost. Valued on Sep-28E P/E (the street's latest method), with EV/EBITDA and DCF (at a WACC) as cross-checks.

build._why: Volumes: FY26 4.21 mt (manufactured 3.57, traded 0.64); Q1FY27 0.985 mt (+4.7%; manufactured 0.86, traded 0.13). FY27: plants run near 70% of phosphoric-acid capacity while sulphur and ammonia are scarce, so manufactured volume slips to ~3.40 mt despite the 0.3 mt granulation debottleneck from Dec-2026; ~0.5 mt of imports secured for rabi lift traded volume to ~0.95 mt. FY28: capacity 4.0 mt and phosphoric acid 0.7 mt from Aug-Sep 2027, manufactured 3.85 mt, trading back to ~0.70 mt. FY29: manufactured 4.05 mt (the debottlenecked 4.0 mt run fully plus a little from the 1.0 mt granulation train, guided for around Q2FY29-FY30), traded 0.75 mt. Revenue per tonne: FY26 ₹51,845, Q1FY27 ₹62,165 (NPK prices +₹400-500 a bag, Kharif NBS +10%, more DAP and imports); FY27 ₹61,000; FY28-29 ₹58,000 as input prices ease partly. EBITDA per tonne (Screener basis): FY25 ₹4,120, FY26 ₹5,245, Q1FY27 ₹7,309 on low-cost stock. FY27 ₹4,900, a touch under management's 'realistic ~₹5,000', because Q2 buys sulphur at $1,000+ and acid at $1,700 against an unchanged Kharif subsidy, rabi rates were unknown and trading (~₹2,000/t) is a bigger share. FY28 ₹5,400 (phase-1 acid, Goa energy savings, debottlenecked volumes) and FY29 ₹5,800: well short of management's ₹6,500-7,000+ after full integration, which needs the big project and normal raw-material prices.

assumptions._revenueWhy: From the build: 4.35 mt × ₹61,000 = ₹26,535 cr (FY27E, +21.6%); 4.55 mt × ₹58,000 = ₹26,390 cr (FY28E, −0.5%); 4.80 mt × ₹58,000 = ₹27,840 cr (FY29E, +5.5%). Price, not volume, drives FY27; volume drives FY29.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 cash capex ₹868 cr (sulphuric acid plants, Goa energy project). FY27 ₹800 cr: '~₹600 cr' normal capex incl. some major-project outflow (CFO, May-2026), ₹600-700 cr per the Jun-2026 plant visit, plus the first ~₹100 cr of the ₹250 cr aluminium fluoride plant. FY28-29 ₹1,600 cr and ₹1,500 cr: most of the ₹3,600 cr programme (1.0 mt granulation, 0.3 mt phosphoric acid with matching sulphuric acid) plus the rest of aluminium fluoride and ~₹200 cr a year of maintenance. Management funds new projects ~70% with debt.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹403 cr = 5.8% of average gross block (₹6,944 cr); Q4FY26 ₹126 cr and Q1FY27 ₹106 cr (~₹424 cr a year) after the new sulphuric acid plants. The engine holds CWIP flat and depreciates capex at once, but most FY28-29 capex is construction work in progress that earns no depreciation until the big project is commissioned (Q2FY29-FY30), so we use 5.3%: ~₹421 / ₹485 / ₹567 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net-debt company: borrowings ₹6,872 cr plus ₹34 cr of leases at Mar-2026 against cash, bank balances and liquid funds of ₹409 cr (net debt ~₹6,500 cr). Interest income is built into other income below, not earned on a treasury book.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, Screener basis (which nets the loss on discarded plant). FY26 company other income ₹147 cr = interest ₹29 cr (bank ₹12 cr, tax refund ₹3 cr, other ₹14 cr) + mutual-fund gains ₹59 cr (parking subsidy receipts) + rent ₹5 cr + miscellaneous ₹50 cr + write-backs ₹4 cr; Screener shows ₹88 cr 'normal' after netting ₹56 cr of plant-discard loss. FY27E ₹85 cr = interest ₹20 cr (cash fell from ₹1,036 cr to ₹392 cr) + fund gains ₹30 cr (smaller surpluses with debt up) + rent and miscellaneous ₹55 cr − discard losses ₹20 cr; write-backs excluded. Check: Q1FY27 normal other income ₹21.6 cr (×4 = ₹86 cr); TTM normal ₹134 cr before Screener's annual netting of discard losses. FY29E ₹90 cr. The +₹21.8 cr Q1FY27 exceptional (Labour Code reversal) is excluded.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (interest, bank charges, exchange loss on foreign-currency borrowings)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹528 cr = interest ₹333 cr + exchange loss on buyer's credit ₹145 cr + bank charges ₹45 cr + tax interest ₹4 cr; Q1FY27 ₹132 cr (~₹527 cr a year) on gross debt of ₹6,500 cr. FY27E ₹540 cr: debt stays high with subsidy receivables at ₹4,600 cr and costlier imports; we assume a smaller exchange loss than FY26. FY28E ₹520 cr: working capital eases but project debt builds, with interest during construction capitalised. FY29E ₹545 cr as project debt peaks (~5.8% on ~₹8,500 cr plus ~₹50 cr of bank charges and ~₹30 cr of exchange cost, less capitalised interest).
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 25.0% (FY26), 25.4% (Q1FY27); new-regime statutory rate 25.17%. Paradeep's merged entity has no minorities (MCFL merged, not a subsidiary), so model EPS = profit ÷ 103.75 cr shares (actual 103.82 cr).
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹1.50 a share (15.6% of EPS); FY25 ₹1.00. Capex years: we assume 15%.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts free cash flow at one rate and labels it the cost of equity. Paradeep carries ~₹6,500-7,500 cr of net debt against a market value of ~₹16,000 cr, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1: subsidy-policy and raw-material risk plus leverage) weighted ~70%, post-tax cost of debt ~6.0% (8% pre-tax at the margin) weighted ~30% = ~11.0%, which is what beta 0.75 produces. The same rate rolls the value forward six months.
dcf._tgWhy: Phosphatic fertiliser demand grows ~2-3% a year in volume plus price; 5.5% nominal in rupees.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~5.5% (FY29E) to 6% by year 12: ~2-3% volume (the 1.0 mt granulation train and acid expansion fill, then market growth) plus ~3% price.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin drifts from 10.0% (FY29E) to 10.5% (~₹6,100/t on ₹58,000/t) as integration completes; policy (NBS, reasonable-margin rules) keeps it below management's ₹7,000/t aspiration.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~5.4% of revenue (FY29E, big project) to 3%, above depreciation at 2.2% to fund volume growth.
dcf._yearsWhy: 12-year explicit/fade period so the FY28-29 project spend is followed by the years in which it earns.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Rabi and FY28 subsidy rates cover the Middle East cost spike, sulphur and ammonia normalise, the big project lands on time and integration lifts EBITDA towards ₹6,500/t by FY29 (management's path); volumes grow faster with the new granulation train.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Subsidy rates lag input costs for another year, sulphur stays above $1,000/t, trading is a larger share, the big project slips and the government tightens reasonable-margin rules: EBITDA stays near ~₹4,500-5,000/t while debt keeps rising.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Paradeep now: Prabhudas Lilladher 13x FY28E EPS (Accumulate, ₹158, 31-Jul-2026; 10-11x in Mar-Jun 2026). 9.5x is derived: the stock's one-year-forward P/E median since listing (May-2022) is 11.6x after putting FY25 EPS on the merger-consistent basis and leaving out the FY24 trough year (10.9x on Screener's unadjusted EPS); seven listed fertiliser peers traded a median 17% below their five-year median P/E on 30-Sep-2026, so 11.6x × 0.83 ≈ 9.6x, rounded to 9.5x. No premium for growth: EPS compounds ~10% a year FY26-29E, ROE (~14%) only matches the ~13% cost of equity and net debt stays near 3x EBITDA. Bull 13x (the street's multiple: the market keeps paying for the integration story); bear 8x (where Chambal, GNFC and GSFC trade: a plain, indebted fertiliser maker under subsidy stress).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Elara Capital's method (8.0x FY28E, May-2026). Paradeep's trailing EV/EBITDA median since listing is 10.0x outside the FY24 trough window; peers traded a median 5% below their five-year EV/EBITDA, i.e. ~9.5x trailing, which on Sep-28E EBITDA (~14% above the trailing twelve months) is ~8.3x: we use 8x and deduct Sep-28E net debt (~₹7,800 cr).
